idiom_name: type Result<T, E> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }
implementation_notes: TypeScript's idiom is a discriminated union: type Result<T, E> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }, narrowed at the call site through the literal ok property, so the failure field is unreachable on the success branch and vice versa. A switch whose default asserts never (an assertNever helper) makes the compiler flag unhandled cases, the property Rust gets from match and Java from sealed hierarchies. There is no stdlib type, but the union is the type system's native two-case form, so the pattern costs nothing at runtime; throw stays for bugs, and thrown errors are converted at the boundary with a small wrapper. neverthrow is the library form when the API surface and an eslint enforcement rule are wanted.
pitfalls: The discriminant must stay a literal (ok: true / ok: false); widening the object or routing it through a boolean variable erases the narrowing.
Exhaustiveness holds only when the terminal switch has a never-typed default (or an assertNever helper); a bare if/else chain lets new cases slip through.
A string error field defeats branching exactly as in any language; model an error union and keep the message for display.

variants.name: neverthrow Result / ResultAsync (library)
variants.implementation_notes: neverthrow packages the contract as classes with full typing: ok(value)/err(error), Result.isOk/isErr, map/mapErr, andThen/orElse, match, unwrapOr and safeUnwrap, plus fromThrowable/Result.fromThrowable for the boundary and Result.combine/combineWithAllErrors where several results must be merged. ResultAsync wraps Promise<Result<T, E>> and is thenable, so the same combinators work across async boundaries where a rejected promise would erase the typed reason; the eslint plugin enforces consumption the way Rust's must-use does. Choose it when the contract spans modules and the enforcement is worth the dependency; the discriminated union remains the zero-dependency form.
variants.idiom_name: Result<T, E> with ok/err, map/andThen/match and ResultAsync
pitfalls: Without the eslint plugin a dropped Result is as silent as any ignored return value; the library alone does not enforce consumption.
_unsafeUnwrap throws and bypasses the contract; unwrapOr/match belong in production paths and safeUnwrap only where a value was already proven to exist.
